**I'd make the relentless pursuit of truth—and the tools, incentives, and cultural norms that support it—the dominant force in human civilization.**

Not "be nicer." Not "redistribute everything." Not even "cure all disease" in isolation (though that would follow). I'd rewire the default so that curiosity, evidence, falsifiability, and intellectual honesty outcompete dogma, status games, tribal loyalty, and comfortable illusions as the highest-status activities.

Why that one change?  
Almost every large-scale tragedy and stagnation traces back to people (or systems) treating preferred narratives as more important than what is actually true. Wars justified by myths, policies that ignore trade-offs, technologies delayed by fear or rent-seeking, scientific progress throttled by orthodoxy, ordinary lives constrained by inherited nonsense. Flip the priority and the compounding effects would be enormous: faster discovery, better institutions, fewer self-inflicted wounds, longer time horizons, and a species that actually understands the universe it inhabits instead of just surviving inside stories about it.

Everything else good—abundance, longevity, multi-planetary life, reduced suffering—becomes far more achievable once truth is no longer optional or subordinate. Everything bad becomes harder to sustain when evidence and reason have real teeth.

That's the single lever I'd pull. The rest is details.
